repeatedSamples.sentence: Before Mina leaves the place, the blue bird notices a small note nearby.
The last line matches the map, so Mina and the bird keep walking.
A little farther on, Mina finds a folded paper beside the red path.
Mina finds another clue just before the path turns.
Mina puts the paper safely in her bag and follows the next mark.
Near the next tree, Mina sees a short message waiting under a stone.
One detail helps Mina understand where they should go next.
The bird chirps at a small card near the road, and Mina stops to read it.
The clue makes the next part of the map easier to follow.
When Mina finishes, she smiles at the bird and they move on together.
A small paper appears near the next mark on the map.
After reading them, Mina checks the red line and starts walking again.
A new picture grows across the paper while Mina and her friends watch.
A warm gold light runs across the next page and reveals another small memory.
Before the page turns again, the storybook shows Mina, Joon, and Sara a few short lines.
Mina smiles when the final line makes the next picture glow.
Mina, Joon, and Sara read it together before the page turns.
The friends talk about what they learned before the light moves on.
The old book opens to a page the friends have not seen before.
The picture becomes bright when the friends understand the message.
When they finish reading, a little star appears near the next page.
The book pauses on another memory from the school.
The friends remember the scene as the golden light moves forward.
A small paper door opens inside the storybook and shows another scene.
A nearby folder contains several short memories from people who once used the garden.
Mina compares the details with the map before the three friends continue.
The new details make the next part of the mystery easier to understand.
They record the useful details and return to the main clue.
A repeated detail links the notes to the larger mystery.
Another envelope contains messages that were saved by people who cared for the garden.
Before leaving the area, Mina finds another bundle connected to the garden’s history, and Joon and Sara help her examine it.
Mina pauses to review another set of notes before they move to the next place.
Near the next location, Joon notices a packet that everyone else had missed.
Sara checks the dates while Mina marks the details that may matter later.
The friends find a small box of records near the path and read the contents in order.
The friends study it together, then continue with a clearer idea of what happened.
Before moving to the next source, Mina reviews another set of Riverside records beside her timeline.
She marks what can be verified and returns to the main investigation.
A second file box gives Mina several accounts that were never explained in the shortened public summary.
Another group of records fills a gap between two dates on Mina’s timeline.
During the supervised review, Mina opens a folder that earlier summaries had reduced to a few lines.
Mina compares another set of documents with the sources she has already collected.
Mina keeps the different accounts visible so the final report will not erase disagreement.
Mina records the source of each claim before connecting it to the larger timeline.
She keeps the conflicting details side by side instead of forcing them into one version.
She notes the points that can be checked against independent evidence.
She separates fact, memory, and opinion before deciding what the material can prove.
The archive index leads Mina to another packet of letters, reports, and interview notes.
